titel: Great Leaders Lead Themselves Well, Part 2

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen (Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst podtrac.com) - zu wenig fuer ein Urteil, aber nicht nichts

einzeiler: Great leadership begins with self-leadership: three core commitments for enduring impact.
kurzfassung: Andy Stanley and Holly Goddard continue their discussion on self-leadership based on the new book What Great Leaders Do. They explore the importance of telling oneself the truth, separating temporary appetites from true values, and inviting external feedback. The conversation highlights practical mental exercises for leaders to align their daily decisions with lifelong principles.
stichpunkte: Commitment one: Refusing self-deception even when the truth feels uncomfortable.
Commitment two: Prioritizing long-term values over temporary appetites for more and now.
Greater organizational authority and influence amplify personal appetites and options.
Asking what one really wants helps bridge the gap between immediate desires and core values.
Discovering personal definition of success through a legacy-focused thought exercise.
Viewing violations of personal values as failure rather than mere mistakes.
Commitment three: Acknowledging that nobody leads themselves well alone and actively inviting input.
Modeling the proper reception of feedback for team members and subordinates.

kapitel.titel: The Third Commitment: Never Leading Alone

clips.text: The speakers explain that holding a position of greater organizational power tends to magnify human desires.
Quoting Patrick Lencioni's early work, the hosts note that a leader's first temptation often involves ego rather than performance.
The conversation shifts to how violating one's own established values represents a significant failure rather than just a casual error.
The host emphasizes that achieving maximum potential requires intentionally bringing other people into one's decision-making process.
Reacting gracefully to critique does more than improve the leader; it demonstrates the exact behavior expected from subordinates.

beschreibung:
The hardest person you'll ever lead is the person you see in the mirror every day. And the more influence you have, the more important self-leadership becomes.
In this episode, Andy Stanley and Holly Goddard continue their conversation on why self-leadership is the foundation of great leadership. They explore why leaders must prioritize what they value most over what they want now, and why leading yourself well requires inviting others in.
